title: Sort Words by Frequency
prompt: A search page wants popular words first. Write a function that returns each unique word sorted by frequency from highest to lowest. If two words have the same frequency, sort them alphabetically.

explanation.beginner:
Example: frequencySort(["js","ts","js","css","ts","js"]) produces ["js","ts","css"]. Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Compare “breaks ties alphabetically”: input [["beta","alpha","beta","alpha","gamma"]] produces ["alpha","beta","gamma"]. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Use a key-specific bucket or count so each occurrence changes only its own group.

Tempting mistake: Reinitializing an existing group erases earlier contributions. Distinct-key counts differ from total occurrences.

The reference uses sort, map. Trace the intermediate value after each operation; count repeated scans inside callbacks separately when estimating cost.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “breaks ties alphabetically”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
